text:
Maya: heads up — the int8 canary we rolled to alpha is returning intermittent non-JSON text appended to funcall outputs. noticed ~0.8% parse failures on the new model vs 0.05% baseline.
Rafael: ugh, numbers? is it trailing commentary or broken structure?
Maya: mostly trailing prose after the JSON blob, sometimes a stray "--" or a short explanatory sentence. example from logs:
```
{"action":"search","args":{"q":"redwood inference"}}
Thanks — hope that helps!
```
Priya: that looks like the model is sometimes emitting a human-style footer. could be temperature/decoding or a special token mapping lost in quantization.
Sam: can you link the canary id? I want to compare mirror outputs.
Maya: canary: canary-2026-03-18-int8-stitch. I mirrored 5000 requests (same prompts) to baseline fp16 and int8. int8 parse_fail_rate=0.82% fp16=0.04%.
Rafael: telemetry — any correlation with sequence length or batch size?
Maya: yes — 75% of failures are >350 tokens. distribution skew to longer responses. also appears more in streaming mode.
Priya: thought: maybe kv-cache prefix merging + quantization rounding causes tokenization boundary shift -> model emits a partial extra sentence after the closing JSON.
Sam: good hypothesis. can we repro deterministically with a short prompt and forced seed?
Maya: tried fixed-seed sampling; still stochastic but higher chance. deterministic greedy reduces but doesn't eliminate.
infra-bot: Canary deployment canary-2026-03-18-int8-stitch -> rollout 15% -> health: degraded (parse_fail_rate up).
Rafael: actionable plan?
Priya: propose triage steps: 1) run targeted A/B on long prompts with streaming disabled, 2) run token-level diff of top-k tokens at closure point, 3) add a post-output sanitizer to strip trailing free-text heuristically for canary.
Sam: also test lowering temperature and enabling strict eos penalties. might nudge model to stop at JSON boundary.
Maya: patch for post-output sanitizer ready: it trims any non-json after first balanced brace and attempts repair heuristics (wrap with [] or add closing brace). quick patch dropped parse_fail_rate to 0.1% in canary sample (but we need to avoid hiding real regressions).
Rafael: important to flag this in onboarding checklist: add a "structured-output sanity" smoke test at sequence lengths up to 1024.
Priya: agree. also file a model-adoption blocker until we understand root cause. add quantization-runbook entry: token-boundary sensitivity test.
Maya: I'll add a telemetry slice for trailing-token signatures and attach sample ids to the canary ticket.
Sam: for short-term, continue sandbox sanitizer + lower temp for canary. long-term, we need root-cause: kernel selection? tokenizer detokenization quirk? compilation kernel rounding?
Priya: pinging @Rafael and @infra-bot to schedule a micro-bisect: run same seed across different kernel sets (avx, cuda-vec, alt-kernel) and compare outputs.
infra-bot: Scheduled job: micro-bisect-token-boundary (canary-2026-03-18-int8-stitch). started.
Maya: thanks. recording action items:
- Maya: attach failing sample set + sanitizer metrics to ticket (in progress).
- Rafael: run kernel micro-bisect and report diffs (ETA today EOD).
- Priya: add structured-output smoke tests to onboarding checklist and quant runbook.
- Sam: run temp/penalty ablations and check streaming vs non-streaming effect.
Rafael: quick ask — do we have a lightweight eval that classifies outputs into (clean JSON / JSON+trailing / malformed)? could run nightly.
Maya: yes, I'll spin up a nightly job that runs 10k examples across models and emits slice metrics.
Priya: cool. if sanitizer is kept, add a debug header so we can count how often it's triggered (don't hide in prod logs).
Maya: will add header: X-StructSanitizer: partial-heuristic-applied.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Maya: will update the canary ticket with initial bisect logs and sample ids when infra-bot finishes.
Rafael: thanks team — prioritize until we hit <0.1% parse failures or have root cause.
Priya: and let's not ship policy papers that mask regressions. short-term guard + long-term fix.
Maya: agreed. finishing notes: looks like quantization introduces subtle tokenization boundary sensitivity especially in long streaming outputs. bisect and kernel comparisons are highest signal next.
Sam: keep the thread updated.
infra-bot: micro-bisect-token-boundary -> completed step 1/6 (pending further runs).
